cards.front: Recall a key point about Regulation & Issues
cards.back: Media regulation involves rules and systems that govern what media content can be produced, distributed, and accessed. It aims to protect audiences while preserving freedom of expression.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Regulation & Issues
cards.back: Ofcom regulates UK broadcasting — setting content standards, protecting audiences from harmful material, ensuring due impartiality in news, and managing the radio/TV spectrum.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Regulation & Issues
cards.back: The BBFC classifies films and some video content (U, PG, 12A, 12, 15, 18). Classification considers discrimination, drugs, horror, imitable behaviour, language, nudity, sex, threat, and violence.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Regulation & Issues
cards.back: IPSO (Independent Press Standards Organisation) regulates most UK newspapers and magazines. It handles complaints and enforces the Editors' Code of Practice, but has been criticised as weak.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Regulation & Issues
cards.back: IMPRESS is an alternative press regulator recognised under the Royal Charter. It has fewer members than IPSO but stronger powers and independence.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Regulation & Issues
cards.back: The ASA (Advertising Standards Authority) regulates advertising across all media. Adverts must be legal, decent, honest, and truthful. The CAP Code covers non-broadcast ads; BCAP Code covers broadcast.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Regulation & Issues
cards.back: The Online Safety Act 2023 requires platforms to protect users from harmful content, particularly children. Ofcom enforces it, with powers including fines of up to 10% of global revenue.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Regulation & Issues
cards.back: Censorship vs regulation: regulation sets rules and standards (age ratings, content warnings); censorship suppresses content entirely. The UK system is primarily regulatory, not censorious.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Regulation & Issues
cards.back: Freedom of expression (Article 10 EHR Act) protects the right to express ideas but has limits — hate speech, defamation, incitement to violence are not protected.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Regulation & Issues
cards.back: Self-regulation vs statutory regulation: the newspaper industry prefers self-regulation (IPSO), arguing it protects press freedom. Critics argue self-regulation lacks teeth and independence.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Regulation & Issues
cards.back: The Leveson Inquiry (2012) investigated press ethics after the phone hacking scandal. Leveson recommended independent regulation with royal charter backing, but most newspapers chose IPSO instead.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Regulation & Issues
cards.back: Global challenges: the internet is borderless, making national regulation difficult. US-based platforms (Google, Meta, X) may resist UK regulation. International cooperation is increasingly necessary.

cards.front: What should you know about media studies exam tips — regulation & issues?
cards.back: 1. For Regulation & Issues, use media terminology precisely (e.g. connotation, denotation, representation, ideology) 2. Always analyse how media language creates meaning for specific audiences 3. Reference specific examples from set products to support your analysis 4. When evaluating Regulation & Issues, consider the role of media industries and cultural contexts 5. For extended answers, debate different interpretations before reaching your own
Evaluate the effectiveness of media regulation in the UK. [15 marks]

AO1 (Knowledge & Understanding): Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of regulation & issues, including key concepts, theories, and media contexts. AO2 (Analysis & Evaluation): Analyse and evaluate regulation & issues using relevant theories and frameworks. Consider different perspectives and reach reasoned conclusions. AO3 (Create): Apply understanding of regulation & issues to practical media
